question: My GWR train was cancelled because of a crew shortage. Can I get compensation?
reference_answer: GWRHelp said compensation may be due depending on the delay, claimed through their link.

answer.answer:
Yes. In late 2017 GWR said a cancellation caused by a shortage of train crew can qualify for money back, but it depends on whether you still travelled and how late you arrived.

If you still travelled, agents said you can claim delay compensation when you were delayed by an hour or more arriving at your destination. They treated crew-shortage cancellations the same way and pointed people to the compensation claim form. Waiting an hour for the next train counted, and the delay is judged on arrival at your final destination, not only on the cancelled train itself. On London and Thames Valley services, compensation started at more than 30 minutes if the journey itself was under an hour. Agents said they do not compensate for delays of 15 minutes.

If you did not travel at all, they said you can claim a full abandoned-journey refund on the unused ticket from the original place of purchase. They said an admin fee applies only if you chose not to travel, not if you abandoned the journey because of disruption.

This is from GWR’s Twitter replies in October–December 2017, so the thresholds may have changed.

verification.feedback: No change needed. Each claim is a fair paraphrase of a GWR agent statement in the cited threads, and the 2017 caveat needs no support.

question: How do I file a discrimination complaint with Delta about how a passenger was treated?
reference_answer: Delta said it does not condone discrimination and pointed to an online complaint form handled by its discrimination specialists.

answer.answer:
Delta’s 2017 Twitter agents described two ways to file a discrimination complaint about how a passenger was treated. The actual form URLs were not saved in those tweets (they appear only as “[link]”), and the process may have changed since then.

**Online complaint form.** Agents told people to file online. In one discrimination case, an agent said you can file a complaint online and a discrimination specialist would investigate [#404321]. When a customer asked to file an official complaint that the treatment was “100% discrimination,” the agent sent a link to do so [#553958]. Separately, agents pointed people to a formal complaint with the Customer Care team / corporate Comment/Complaint form [#798928] [#186177]. If the online form failed or a filed case needed follow-up, agents gave Corporate Customer Care at 800-455-2720 (one agent said prompt 1/4), Monday–Friday, 8 a.m. to 9 p.m. ET, and said they can pull a file or that a review can take time [#186177] [#500483] [#604628].

**Report it on Twitter so they escalate it.** Agents also asked people to follow and DM details so they could forward the incident for investigation—typically the flight confirmation, and sometimes ticket number, email, phone, attendant’s name, and names of people involved. In one case the agent also asked which flight it was [#527446] [#141615] [#406497] [#377811] [#191806]. They said they would send that to Inflight Leadership or the appropriate department. Agents stated that Delta does not condone or tolerate discrimination and that they investigate internally [#404321] [#141615] [#377811] [#527446].

If the issue is another passenger’s conduct rather than Delta staff, one agent instead suggested a formal complaint with local law enforcement [#686063]. That was not described as Delta’s discrimination-complaint process.

verification.feedback: No changes needed. Each procedural claim is a fair paraphrase of something a Delta agent said in the cited threads.

question: UPS tracking says my package was transferred to the post office. When will it arrive?

- One agent said a transfer to the post office “means they will be delivering the package to you within 1-2 days.” [#615114]
- Another said it “can usually take 1-2 days for the Post Office to make the final delivery,” and to reach out to the shipper with further questions. [#580662]

When customers said a package had already been sitting at the post office—one for 3 days, one for a week—agents recommended contacting the post office directly [#497203], or contacting the shipper or the post office [#768396].

In a separate case where the customer said USPS had not received the package, an agent said it was still in transit to the local post office and to notify the sender if it was not delivered the next day [#580662].

This is based on UPS Twitter support replies from October–November 2017 and may have changed since.

question: My UPS shipment to Kuwait is stuck in customs. Can UPS do anything?
reference_answer: UPSHelp said customs clearance is out of UPS's control; the shipper had been contacted to provide documentation and you need to contact the shipper for updates.

answer.answer:
In 2017, UPS Twitter support treated a shipment stuck in Kuwait customs as largely outside UPS’s control, because clearance is handled by government customs.

In one Kuwait case, after the customer messaged the tracking number, an agent said the package was “in government customs pending release,” that “no further action needs to be taken on your end or ours,” and that UPS was simply waiting for release. They said they would update a new delivery date once the package was back in UPS’s possession [#677438].

In another Kuwait case, the agent said the package had not cleared customs, that this was “out of the control of UPS,” that the shipper had already been contacted to provide documentation, and that the customer needed to contact the shipper for an update [#708180].

That matches what agents said about customs holds more generally: customs is government-run, so UPS cannot control how long a package is held, and customers were told to keep tracking and sign up for notifications [#591131][#726060]. If clearance depends on paperwork, agents told customers to contact the shipper, who can help get the items cleared [#536067][#708180]. In one customs-delay case (not identified as Kuwait), an agent asked the customer to send contact information so the local team could follow up [#356715]. In another case a customer said a UPS team had called asking for documents to be emailed; the agent did not confirm that or say UPS would chase the paperwork—they only asked when the customer was contacted and whether blank documentation for submission had been sent [#726060].

So, based on these 2017 replies: UPS said they cannot speed up or control Kuwait (or other) government customs. When documentation was the issue, they pointed people to the shipper rather than saying UPS would clear it. They sometimes offered to have a local team follow up if you provided contact details, or to check a tracking number you sent them, but in the Kuwait customs case they checked, they concluded nothing further could be done until customs released the package. Policies and local processes may have changed since 2017.

verification.feedback: No fix needed. Each factual claim is a fair paraphrase of a UPS agent statement in the cited conversations, and the 2017 caveat does not require support.

question: American Airlines moved me out of the Main Cabin Extra seat I paid for. Do I get a refund?
reference_answer: American said it sometimes has to make last-minute seat changes and would refund the Main Cabin Extra charge after travel is complete.

answer.answer:
Yes. In 2017, American Airlines agents said that if you paid for a Main Cabin Extra seat and did not sit in it, you should get that charge back—though they described the process in slightly different ways.

- One agent said you should automatically receive a refund if you paid for a Main Cabin Extra seat which you didn’t use, and asked you to DM your record locator [#64329]. That reply did not give a timeline.
- Separately, when a customer said they were bumped from extra legroom they had paid for and had not been refunded, an agent said that if you end up not sitting in a purchase-type seat, you should receive a credit on your account within 2 billing cycles [#180813]. That was described as a credit, not as an automatic refund, and was not tied specifically to the “Main Cabin Extra” wording.
- If you were moved after check-in (when the reservation is locked for airport control), an agent said that if “our agent” can’t find you the same type of seat, they will gladly refund the seat cost. They also said they could not instead refund the person who was put in your seat [#707422].
- When a customer was bumped from a paid extra seat and said customer service would not give a refund, an AmericanAir agent asked them to DM so they could see about setting up a refund for the charge [#90540].
- When a customer asked how to get money back after being bumped out of a Main Cabin Extra seat, an agent apologized that the seat was moved and asked them to DM the record locator so they could take a look [#796418]. They did not explicitly confirm a refund in that reply.

This is from October–December 2017 and may have changed since.

question: My Sainsbury's online order came with a poor substitute. What are my options?
reference_answer: sainsburys said the store sends the closest available match to what you ordered and you can send it back if you're unhappy with it.

answer.answer:
Based on what Sainsbury’s support agents said in 2017, these are your options if an online grocery order arrived with a poor substitute.

**Return it.** Agents said that if you’re unhappy with a substituted product you can return it with the driver for a full refund. One agent, told the substitute was what the store had available, said the customer would need to return those items to store. They did not offer to send the original item or the quantity ordered.

**If the driver has already left.** Agents often asked whether you accepted the substitute or handed it back to the driver, and sometimes whether it was shown on the receipt or paperwork. They then asked customers to DM the order number plus the account name, address and email so they could look into it. The history doesn’t show a guaranteed refund once the driver has gone. Separately, an agent said perishables generally can’t be returned to store — only to the driver during delivery — though that was about a non-substitute return.

**Price difference.** If a substitute costs more than the original, agents said you’ll receive an e-voucher for the difference (one agent said the day after delivery). They said they don’t offer a service where a more expensive substitute costs no more than the item you ordered. If the substitute was cheaper and you were charged more, an agent said the difference is an automatically generated e-voucher to take off your next online shop, and that they cannot refund it to your card. Agents also said they try to keep substitute prices low.

**Next time.** You can decline substitutions in your account settings, or in the basket choose which items may be substituted and which you’d rather not.

This is from Sainsbury’s Twitter support in October–December 2017 and may have changed.

verification.feedback: No fix needed. Each option is tied to something a Sainsbury’s agent said (or a fair paraphrase), and limits such as no guaranteed refund after the driver leaves and the perishables note are accurately caveated.

question: Why does Hulu play so many commercials during some shows?
reference_answer: hulu_support said ad breaks typically happen in the same time slots as in the original broadcast.

answer.answer:
In 2017, Hulu support gave a few related reasons why some shows have a lot of commercials.

Ads on the Limited Commercials plan help keep the price down—agents said ads let them offer new shows at $7.99/month [#502622][#599618][#680662]. They also said they try to keep ads to a modest or reasonable length, but length varies by several factors [#502622][#206033][#775095].

Where the breaks fall follows the original airing: ad breaks typically occur in the same time slots as the original broadcast [#802416][#157704][#292757]. For The Orville, an agent said that would be about five commercial breaks [#802416]. Some agents added that the ad load is lighter than the original airing [#382264][#292757]. Ad load also varies by show and network, among other factors [#671261].

If the commercials themselves are the problem, agents pointed people to a No Commercials plan or add-on [#604032][#368195]. Even that plan was not fully ad-free: due to streaming rights, a small handful of shows still played an ad before and after the episode [#809285].

This is what Hulu agents said in late 2017; the ad model may have changed since.

verification.feedback: No fix needed. Each factual claim is said or fairly paraphrased by a Hulu agent in at least one cited conversation, and the 2017 note needs no citation.

question: Sainsbury's stopped selling a product I really like. Can I ask them to bring it back?
reference_answer: They confirmed the product is no longer stocked and said you can log a product request through their link.

answer.answer:
Yes. In 2017, Sainsbury’s Twitter agents told customers who wanted a discontinued product back that they could log a product request (via a link they shared in replies). That request is meant to show the store and buyers that customers want the item restocked, and agents said buyers would look into it.

It is not a guarantee. One agent said a product request “doesn’t guarantee we’ll get the product back in stock,” but it does show buyers that customers would like it restocked. Another said that if you don’t fill in the request, buyers don’t know customers want the item back. In one case, after a customer said they had already submitted the form many times, an agent logged it with buyers for internal review.

When explaining why an item had gone, agent Rob listed reasons such as shop space, product selling history, and the manufacturer having stopped the product. Sometimes an item is only discontinued at one store, not everywhere, so it can be worth checking another store.

The specific request link from those tweets isn’t preserved in the history, and this process is from late 2017, so it may have changed.

verification.feedback: No changes needed; each claim is a fair paraphrase of what Sainsbury’s agents said in the cited conversations.

question: How do I report a Lyft driver who was driving dangerously?
reference_answer: AskLyft pointed to its Critical Response Line (click 'Call Me' and enter your number on their page) and said you can also report it through the Help Center.

answer.answer:
In October–December 2017, Lyft agents directed people reporting dangerous or reckless driving to a phone callback, usually through Lyft’s Critical Response Line. The links themselves are not preserved in these tweets, and the process may have changed since 2017.

When riders asked how to report a reckless or dangerous driver, agents said to click the “Call Me” button and enter your number at the link they sent, to be immediately connected with the Critical Response Line ([#432064], [#412666], [#301824]). They used that same wording for a driver described as speeding, not using a turn signal, and driving recklessly ([#301558]).

Other replies were close but not identical. For a driver who was all over the road and braking hard, an agent said to report it to the Critical Response Line by clicking the “Call Me” button and entering a number, without saying the caller would be immediately connected ([#803577]). Some agents said only to tap the “Call Me” button to reach the Critical Response Line, without mentioning entering a number ([#18458], [#786136]). For a rider whose driver was “driving mad reckless,” an agent said to click “Call Me” and enter a number to report it, and did not name the Critical Response Line ([#17902]). For erratic driving that included speeding and tailgating, an agent said to click the pink “Call Me” button and enter a callback number to report the ride to the Support Team ([#778185]). When a rider said a driver was going very fast, an agent said to report the ride to the Critical Response Line at a link, without mentioning a Call Me button ([#98740]).

You can also report after the ride. An agent told a rider that calling the Critical Response Line after a ride ends works, and that the line can locate the ride ([#523931]).

verification.feedback: No changes needed; each procedural claim matches an AskLyft agent’s wording or a fair paraphrase, and the citations are accurate.

This is from Southwest’s Twitter support in 2017 and may have changed.

question: I've already used most of my O2 data a week into the month. How can I work out why?
reference_answer: O2 suggested checking your remaining balance on My O2, whether Wi-Fi Assist is turned on, and which apps use the most data.

answer.answer:
O2’s agents in these late-2017 chats said they cannot see what the data was used on. Usage is taken directly from the SIM and they treat that figure as correct, so they can’t itemise it for you ([#102796], [#174871], [#439724]).

What they told people who had burned through data early to do themselves:

- **Check the phone’s data settings.** On an iPhone: Settings → Mobile Data, then scroll down to see which apps have used the most data ([#102796], [#615416], [#544252]).
- **Check the allowance on My O2.** One agent asked whether the usage showed on My O2 and said usage is taken directly from the SIM, so it would be correct ([#174871]). Another said to use My O2 rather than the phone’s own settings for usage info ([#795408]). A separate reply said the figure from the SIM is right and the phone’s own counter isn’t accurate, without naming My O2 ([#103968]).
- **Wi-Fi Assist.** Agents asked whether it was turned on ([#140361], [#391252], [#439724]). One said it is at the bottom of Mobile Data settings ([#439724]), and one told a customer to switch it off ([#615416]). They did not explain in these chats how it uses data.
- **Background apps.** One agent asked whether apps had been running in the background ([#615416]).
- **Software updates.** An agent asked whether any updates had been done that month ([#391252]). Another asked if the phone was on the latest software and said that can affect data usage on the device ([#544252]).
- **Anything else new.** One agent asked if it was the first time this had happened, whether any new services were in use, and whether the phone was on Wi-Fi where possible ([#439724]).

If the allowance ran down very quickly, they also said the usual 80% warning text might not have been sent, and to keep an eye on My O2 rather than waiting for that text ([#323142]).

They often pointed people at a data-usage or data-saving guide (the links are no longer in these tweets) and, if it happens often, at adding a bolt-on or raising the monthly allowance in My O2 ([#102796], [#503064], [#563925]).

This is what O2 support said in October–December 2017, so menu names and My O2 may have changed since.

verification.feedback: No fix needed. Each claim is said by an O2 agent in a cited chat, or is a fair paraphrase, and the 2017 dating note needs no citation.

question: The Crunchyroll app on my Xbox One keeps closing by itself. What should I try?
reference_answer: Uninstall the app, power cycle the Xbox One and the router/modem, then reinstall. If it continues, XboxSupport asked for Detailed Network Statistics (Settings > Network > Network Settings > Detailed Network Statistics).

answer.answer:
In 2017, Xbox Support did not give one fixed sequence for a Crunchyroll app on Xbox One that closes by itself. Agents in different threads suggested different next steps (this may have changed since):

- In one thread where the app loaded and then returned to Home, they first pointed to their app-crash guide. When that and other apps still worked, they said to delete the app, power cycle, then reinstall, in that order. After that still failed and the customer confirmed it was the only app affected, they sent another set of linked steps. When uninstall and reinstall still sent the customer to Home, they said to factory reset the console so it would redownload the latest system update, and on step 7 to choose “Reset and keep my games & apps” [#15843].

- In another thread where the app kept starting and then closing, they said to uninstall the app, power cycle the Xbox One and the router/modem, and reinstall the app. After the customer said that (plus signing out of the app on a laptop) did not help, they asked whether other apps did the same and asked for Detailed Network Stats from Settings > Network > Network Settings > Detailed Network Statistics. They did not ask for a gamertag in that thread, and they did not say to send stats only if Crunchyroll was the only affected app [#82817].

- Where the app opened and closed almost immediately, they pointed to their app-issue guide. After the customer said they had already tried everything on that list, they said to contact the app’s publisher [#242683].

- When someone asked if there was a plan to fix months of Crunchyroll crashes, the agent asked them to DM Xbox Support with their gamertag and the steps they had already tried. That was a request to DM Xbox, not a referral to Crunchyroll [#599946].

The linked guides themselves are not quoted in these tweets, so the exact steps inside those links are not in the history.

verification.feedback: No fix needed. Each troubleshooting step and the negative claims match what Xbox Support agents said in the cited threads.

question: How do I complain about a rude Uber Eats delivery person?
reference_answer: Uber_Support said to tap the 'Help' button in the app; if you've already done that, DM them your account email so they can follow up.

answer.answer:
In October–November 2017, Uber support’s consistent advice was to file the complaint in writing, not by phone.

For a rude Uber Eats delivery person specifically, agents told customers to send a note through their help link so the team could get in touch and look into it. That was the reply both when someone said their UberEATS driver was rude [#493496] and when someone said a delivery driver was rude and ruined their dinner [#144697]. The same “send a note via the help link” instruction was used for other Uber Eats driver problems, such as a missing part of an order [#390209].

They did not give a customer-care phone number for this. When someone asked where to complain about a rude driver and whether there was a phone line, the agent only pointed them to the help link [#233267]. In a related thread, an agent said they did not offer phone support for these issues and to use the link instead [#404062].

Agents also sometimes asked people to direct-message them, but the details differed:
- One agent asked for a DM with the email address and more details so they could connect [#370232].
- Another asked for a DM with the email and phone number linked to the account [#214381].
- When someone wanted to report a rude driver who was not their own, the agent asked for a DM with the email address so they could connect [#749717].

In the app, when the ride is over, you can rate the driver and also leave a comment [#404062]. Agents said that about a ride, not specifically about an Uber Eats delivery. If the rating option does not appear, they still told people to send the details through the help link [#199651].

On what happens after a report, the only statement in these threads was about a cab driver, not an Uber Eats courier: the agent said that under their privacy policy they could not share what action was taken against the driver, but that the team was reviewing the report and would address it [#679499].

The actual form URLs were not preserved in these transcripts (they show up only as “[link]”). This is from October–November 2017 and the process may have changed.

verification.feedback: No fix needed. Each procedural claim is a fair paraphrase of an Uber_Support reply in the cited thread, and the 2017 caveat does not require support.

question: I bought a faulty product at Tesco but can't take it back to the store. Can I still get a refund?
reference_answer: Yes. Tesco can refund from Twitter: DM your name, address and email plus product details (barcode, supplier code, store), choose a refund by email or post, and they may pass your details to the supplier.

answer.answer:
Yes. In late 2017 Tesco’s Twitter agents did issue refunds for faulty or poor-quality products without asking the customer to bring the item back to a store.

They usually sent a Tesco Moneycard by post or email, and asked the customer to DM details first. For an already-opened product, an agent offered a Moneycard by post or email and asked for full name, address, email, barcode, date code, supplier code, and a picture of the receipt, plus permission to pass details to the supplier. They also said that if the customer preferred to return the product on a later visit, store colleagues could arrange an exchange [#789974]. For undercooked baked goods, an agent offered a refund by post or email (they did not call it a Moneycard) and asked for full name, address, email, barcode, store, and price paid [#527943]. For an out-of-date flatbread, an agent offered a Tesco Moneycard by email or post and asked for full name, address, postcode, store, barcode, and price [#650225]. Other agents used the same Moneycard offer for a product they called “very strange” [#271098] and for a product with a poor amount of beef [#634338], again asking for name, address, email, barcode, price or codes, and store, and sometimes a receipt photo and permission to contact the supplier.

If a store visit is possible, agents also directed people that way. One said a return can be made at any store with the same range [#339219]. Another said to return a faulty charger to the store with the receipt so staff could swap it or refund it [#432753].

This is from Tesco’s Twitter support in October–December 2017 and may have changed since.

The agents in #271098 and #634338 both asked for name, address, email, barcode, price or codes, and store, and sometimes a receipt photo and permission to contact the supplier.

question: My FIFA 18 disc won't load on Xbox even though I have the full game. What do I do?
reference_answer: Delete FIFA 18, power cycle the console, then reinstall the game.

answer.answer:
In 2017, Xbox Support’s advice for a FIFA 18 disc that wouldn’t load even though the full game was on the disc was to delete FIFA 18, power cycle the console, then reinstall the game. That customer also said none of their disc games would load, and the agent still gave those same steps [#377295].

Other agents handled similar FIFA 18 disc problems differently. Some pointed people to Xbox’s guide for disc-reading issues [#285405] or the steps for Xbox One disc errors [#357841]. One asked the customer to follow Xbox Support and DM their Gamertag plus more details [#137960].

In a longer case where FIFA 18 still wasn’t recognized, the advice came in stages. After the customer said the disc-recognition guide didn’t work, the agent suggested contacting the retailer for an exchange. When the customer then asked if they could download the installation instead of installing from the disc, the agent said there is only one installation process and it starts when you insert the disc (a digital purchase would still need to install before play). After the customer had exchanged the disc, followed the install guide, and power cycled with no change, the agent sent them to chat support [#203320].

These replies are from October–November 2017 and may not match current Xbox support steps.

verification.feedback: No changes needed. Each advice step matches or fairly paraphrases an Xbox Support agent in the cited conversation, and the 2017 date note needs no support.

question: Miles from one leg of my Delta trip vanished from my SkyMiles account. What can I do?
reference_answer: Delta agents resubmitted the flight for credit and sent a review request to the SkyMiles team, promising an update.

answer.answer:
In a 2017 case almost like yours, a customer said miles from a previous leg had disappeared from the SkyMiles account. The first agent said the credit had been pending and should already have posted, and that they had resubmitted it. After the customer clarified which leg it was, a second agent said they would submit the request to the SkyMiles team for review and would update the customer once they had news [#346777]. Another customer whose status miles were deleted was asked to DM their SkyMiles number so an agent could look [#337933].

Agents also described these other steps, and they did not all say the same thing:

1. **Wait for posting.** One agent said Delta-operated flights can take up to 24 hours after travel is complete, and partner-operated flights up to 7 business days [#263286]. Another said mileage can take 7–10 days, and offered to double-check if the customer shared a SkyMiles number and/or confirmation number by DM [#204075]. For partner flights, other agents said about 30 business days [#241281] or up to six weeks [#44947].

2. **Request the credit yourself.** One agent said you can retroactively add mileage credit once logged into your SkyMiles account, and that you need the ticket numbers of the previous flights, which begin with “006” [#769274]. When that customer saw zeros after entering the ticket number, the agent said that once you request credit the zeros populate, and eligible miles are posted within 7 business days [#769274]. When a customer got credit for only one of two segments, an agent pointed them to a link to file a request for the missing credit [#629121]. When a recent trip showed 0 miles, an agent said to request miles from a past-dated flight by filling out an online form [#793681].

3. **Have an agent look it up.** Agents asked for a SkyMiles number and ticket number via a link so they could assist [#561046], or a SkyMiles number and/or confirmation number by DM so they could double-check [#204075]. They did not say they would resubmit in those two threads. Resubmission is what the first agent said they had already done in the disappeared-leg case [#346777], and what an agent did when part of a ticket showed “activity not eligible for mileage credit”: that agent resubmitted the ticket to SkyMiles for retro credit and said to allow 7 days [#824157]. After a customer sent a SkyMiles number and a ticket number starting with 006, another agent said to allow 7–10 business days for all eligible SkyMiles to post [#97200].

4. **If a leg shows “not eligible.”** In one thread an agent looked at the account and said they were able to fix it so the customer would get proper credit for that leg [#513726]. In a different thread, where the app said the activity was not eligible, the agent called it Delta’s error and said the miles would post within 48 hours [#138716]. The customer later reported the same error on the return leg; the reply in that thread did not say it had been corrected [#138716].

5. **Fax, from one agent only.** That agent said SkyMiles is a self-monitored program, so discrepancies should be faxed and explained to the SkyMiles support desk at (404) 773-1945 [#312133]. Other agents in these threads used a DM, a ticket lookup, or an online request instead.

6. **If the missing leg was on a partner airline.** An agent said SkyMiles should be added to the reservation before departure when traveling with partner airlines [#82669]. In another thread the customer said they had already filled out a request form for Korean Air flights and then posted their SkyMiles number in the thread after being asked to share it via a link. The agent then queued the Korean Air ticket, said to allow 7 days for the SkyMiles to appear, and noted that with partner-airline travel it can take a few extra weeks for the miles to be credited [#699062].

All of this is from Delta’s Twitter support in late 2017, so the form, fax number, and posting times may have changed.

verification.feedback: No fix needed. Each step, timeline, and quote is a fair paraphrase of a Delta agent in the cited thread, and the 2017 caveat needs no support.

question: Spotify put an album by a different artist with the same name on my favourite band's page. How do I report it?
reference_answer: SpotifyCares asked for the album's Spotify URI (right-click the album > Share > URI) so they could correct the artist page.

answer.answer:
In October–November 2017, Spotify’s Twitter support treated a same-name album mix-up as something you report to them by sending identifiers, after which they said they would report it internally.

When someone asked how to report an album attributed to the wrong band with the same name, the agent asked for the URIs of the artist pages and the album that should be on a separate page, then said “We’ll get this reported” once those were sent [#399234]. Other agents asked for the same kind of pair: the URI of the artist page and the albums that should be on a separate page, and said they would investigate once they had that [#596423]; the URIs of the correct artist page and the albums that should be on a separate page [#282418]; or the URIs of the artist pages and the albums that should be on separate pages [#577346]. After the customer sent those, agents in [#282418] and [#577346] said they would get it reported ([#282418] also later said they had reported the extra albums). In [#303453] the agent asked for the Spotify URIs of the bands/albums being discussed and, after the customer described which releases were the other band, said they would report it. In [#629706] the agent only asked for the URI of the album, then said they would report it once that was sent. In [#303213], a listener who could not find the URI on mobile sent a normal link, and the agent still said they would report it.

How agents said to copy a URI:
- Artist page: click “...” next to the artist name, then Share, then Copy Spotify URI [#73428]. Another agent said click the 3 dots below the artist name, then Share, then Copy Spotify URI [#303213].
- Album: right-click the album, then Share, then Copy Spotify URI [#629706] [#32327].
- Track: right-click the track, then Share, then URI [#577346]. One agent also said tap the three dots, then Share, then Copy Spotify URI [#280067].

When the person contacting them was the artist whose page had another artist’s releases on it, some agents told them to contact their distributor so the distributor could work with Spotify (CD Baby in [#352340]) [#352340] [#280067]. In [#280067] the customer then sent links to the tracks, and the agent still said they would report them; later that thread they again suggested the distributor and Spotify’s Artist Support team. Separately, for artist bios—not the mixed albums—[#303453] said only the artists themselves or their label/distributor could request updates or corrections.

This is what agents said in 2017; the steps may have changed since.

verification.feedback: No fix needed. Each reporting step, URI instruction, and artist-vs-fan distinction matches what SpotifyCares agents said in the cited threads, and the 2017 caveat needs no citation.

This is what their support agents told customers in October–December 2017, so the practice or how they explain it may have changed since.

question: I keep getting disconnected at the end of Call of Duty WWII matches on Xbox and lose my XP. Is it my connection?
reference_answer: XboxSupport said it appeared to be a known issue that Activision was investigating, and offered to help troubleshoot the network connection too.

answer.answer:
Activision support did not tell people this was their connection. In November 2017, when players reported a “disconnected from server” (or lost connection to host) at the end of Call of Duty: WWII matches, agents called it a known issue the studio was aware of and investigating, and pointed them to a status page for updates. That includes replies to players who said they were on Xbox One. Agents did not confirm the XP loss, losses, or missing orders those players described. [400655] [472250] [481302] [485103] [503095] [524346] [532751] [548794]

They still asked some people to check the connection before or while reporting it: unplug the console and router for 5 full minutes and play 2–3 matches, say whether the connection is wired or wireless, and send a screenshot of connection speeds [400655]; restart the router and platform for a few minutes, verify cache (not “clear cache”), then DM upload and download speeds [487074]; or DM region, platform, and whether you are on a wired connection [516474]. Xbox Support, after a player said the drop was from the game server back to HQ rather than from Xbox Live, asked for a picture of Settings > Network > Detailed Network Statistics. They did not say that ruled out a console or connection problem. [538745]

On fixes, agents said early in November that server issues should be resolved and asked if people were still seeing them [420366] [435838]. On 22 November an agent said the latest updates had addressed end-of-game server disconnects and to DM if you still could not play. The agent did not confirm a later update brought the problem back. [612565]

This is from November 2017 support replies, so it may have changed since.

verification.feedback: No fix needed. The cited agent replies support the known-issue responses, connection checks, Xbox network-stats request, and fix statements, and the negatives match what those agents did not confirm.

question: British Airways lost my suitcase on my flight to New York. Can I claim for essentials I have to buy?
reference_answer: Yes. BA said to check the delayed bag's status through its link and send receipts for essentials bought while without your bags so they can arrange reimbursement.

answer.answer:
Yes. In 2017 British Airways agents said that if your bag has not arrived and you are away from home, you can buy essential items and claim for them. That is reimbursement of those purchases, not a separate compensation payment for the delay itself.

What they told passengers:
- Buy the essentials you need and keep all receipts. They said they can reimburse or “contribute towards” essentials bought while you are waiting, and that claims are assessed or reviewed.
- As examples of what you may buy, one agent named clothing, toiletries, a bathing suit, and sun lotion, and said the receipts would be assessed once you return.
- Submit the receipts (often via the baggage-claim link they sent, or by DM with your WorldTracer reference, full name, home address, email, and receipts). They recommended sending all receipts together once the bag is back, rather than claiming as you buy each item. If you are still away, they still told people to buy what they need and keep the receipts for a claim on return.
- There is a maximum liability under the Montreal Convention, but agents said that amount fluctuates and did not give a fixed figure. They advised keeping costs as low as you reasonably can.
- They also said they do not offer compensation just because a bag was delayed. Reimbursement is for essential purchases while you were without your belongings and away from home. In one case an agent confirmed a baggage claim had been sorted, without describing what was paid.

This is from British Airways Twitter support in October–December 2017, so the process or limits may have changed. Report the bag (WorldTracer) if you have not already, and keep the receipts.

question: How do I change the Wi-Fi name and password on my Safaricom fibre router?

question: How do I stop Safaricom promotional text messages?
reference_answer: Dial *100# or *200#, choose Products and Services, then option 98 'Stop Safaricom Promotion SMS', and follow the prompts.

answer.answer:
Safaricom agents in late 2017 treated this as two different kinds of texts, and the opt-out steps depend on which you are getting. These menus are from 2017 and may have changed.

**Safaricom’s own promotional SMS** (what agents called “Safaricom promotion SMS” or “our Promotional messages”):
- On prepaid, dial *100#. On postpaid, dial *200# [#514388] [#775178].
- Go to Products & Services, then 98 (more), then Stop Safaricom Promotion SMS, and follow the prompts [#572335] [#660672] [#620752] [#514388] [#573434]. One agent said to reply NO to stop [#501394].
- After a successful unsubscribe, agents said you should no longer get those promotional notifications. If the menu errors or texts keep coming, DM them your number and they can turn the promos off (in one case, effective from midnight) [#514388] [#602855] [#501394] [#216073].

**Marketing texts from other companies** (a named sender, not Safaricom):
- Dial *100# or *200#, then My subscriptions > Marketing messages, and follow the prompts to unsubscribe. You may need to enter the sender name [#602855] [#500805] [#622411] [#775178].
- A shorter path one agent gave: dial *100*5# or *200*5#, reply Marketing Messages, then Deactivate promotion SMS, and enter the sender name. You should get a confirmation text [#687692].
- In the My Safaricom app: Services > My SMS Services, then deactivate the active ones [#775178].
- If the keypad will not let you type the sender name, try another handset [#622411].

Agents distinguished these marketing texts from premium-rate (PRS) SMS; one said a message of this kind was a marketing text, not a PRS SMS [#622411].

question: My Virgin Trains service was late and I couldn't sit in my reserved seat. Can I claim compensation?
reference_answer: Yes. VirginTrains said you can claim compensation online through their link.

answer.answer:
Yes, based on what Virgin Trains agents said in 2017, you can claim for a reserved seat you couldn’t use, and separately for a late arrival if the delay was long enough.

**Reserved seat.** If you reserved a seat and were unable to use it (for example seats showed as unreserved, or the train was too crowded to reach the seat), agents said you may be eligible for compensation and asked people to raise a claim with the Customer Resolutions team via their online form. They said compensation is only available if you had a reserved seat and did not receive it; without a reservation they would not issue compensation for standing, because trains are designed for standing when overcrowded. They did not quote a fixed amount. In one case a customer who stood nearly two hours after missing a reserved seat was told that £5 was the compensation for that issue, and that the ticket purchased is for travel.

**Late train.** Delay Repay is available if you were delayed by more than 30 minutes. A delay of 29 minutes 43 seconds was refused because it did not reach 30 minutes. Claim it via the Delay Repay form. Automatic Delay Repay depends on the ticket; otherwise Customer Resolutions can take up to 28 days to reply. Compensation is only for the train ticket, not for missed meetings or other knock-on costs.

This is from Virgin Trains’ Twitter support in late 2017 and may have changed.

question: Songs I listen to every day suddenly disappeared from Spotify and my playlist. Why?
reference_answer: SpotifyCares said content is sometimes temporarily removed because of licensing changes and hopefully will be available again soon.

answer.answer:
In 2017, Spotify support’s usual explanation was licensing. When songs people listened to regularly suddenly vanished from Spotify and from their playlists, agents said content is sometimes removed temporarily because of licensing changes, and in at least one case also “other legal issues.” They said licensing agreements affect what music is available, including by country, and they hoped the tracks would come back, without promising when. They often pointed people to a help article about Spotify content.

That same answer came up for songs that disappeared from a user’s own playlist and from the catalogue, tracks that went greyed out, and individual songs missing from albums. Examples include someone who said they listened to the missing tracks daily [#673533], tracks removed from a playlist and the catalogue [#188050], songs no longer on a playlist [#163548] [#232105] [#398946], greyed-out tracks that support confirmed had been removed temporarily [#197712], and songs or albums that were no longer playable [#536856] [#75319] [#419947] [#530943]. Region limits were also described as coming down to licensing [#194042]. This is from late 2017 and may have changed.

question: A PS4 trophy I earned won't unlock even after reinstalling the game. What can I do?
reference_answer: AskPlayStation suggested using Restore Licenses to refresh your purchases.

answer.answer:
In 2017, PlayStation Support’s usual first public step when a trophy would not unlock was to sync trophies manually. One agent spelled that out as: go to Trophies, press Options, and choose Sync with PlayStation Network [#351667]. Other threads gave the same sync advice, often via a link [#616359] [#348804] [#541322] [#236580] [#300640].

In the only thread where a customer said they had already reinstalled the game and repeating the unlock still did not award the trophy, that note came after the sync suggestion. There was no further public reply from the agent after the reinstall note [#541322].

If syncing did not help, some agents next suggested Restore Licenses to refresh purchases. Only one thread stated the menu path: Settings > Account Management > Restore Licenses [#566649]. In another, the agent only linked Restore Licenses after the customer said a manual sync (game off and on) did not work; the customer never said they restored licenses [#300640].

When sync alone did not fix it, agents often moved the case off the public thread: they said they had already sent a Twitter DM [#616359], or told the customer to check DMs [#236580]. In [#236580] that came after the customer said they had already synced and had no error code. In [#616359] it came after the customer said the trophy still would not unlock following the sync advice. A similar “check your DMs” reply was given when a trophy went missing after a move from PS4 to PS4 Pro and a manual sync did not bring it back [#35200] — a different situation from a trophy that never unlocked.

In the Minecraft thread, the customer had already tried syncing (plus clearing cache and a new world). After they restored licenses and the trophies still did not pop, the agent said they had sent a DM with further instructions [#566649]. Separately, in the South Park thread, after the customer said they might not pursue the missing trophy, the agent asked them to follow PlayStation Support on Twitter and say when they had, so support could send a DM [#300640].

These replies are from PlayStation Support tweets in October–November 2017, so the steps may have changed.

question: My phone with my Virgin Trains mobile tickets might be dead by the time I travel. What can I do?
reference_answer: VirginTrains said you must be able to display mobile tickets on your device, and suggested contacting the Aftersales team to see if they could be sent to another device.

answer.answer:
Virgin Trains agents in 2017 said a mobile ticket has to be displayed on your device when you travel. If your phone is dead and you can’t show the ticket, they said you would need to buy another one. They told one customer in that exact situation that they can’t change the delivery method once the ticket has been purchased, and that going to the station wouldn’t avoid buying a replacement [#219597].

What they did suggest, if you still have time before travel:
- If you are travelling with someone else, or you have another phone/device, contact Aftersales and ask them to resend the ticket to that other device. Agents gave the number 0344 556 5650, and also pointed people to Websupport LiveChat [#219597][#268207][#819137][#603964].
- If you only have a laptop and no other phone, agents said you would likely still need to buy another ticket, but advised calling Aftersales anyway in case they can do something else [#268207][#819137].
- Changing an e-ticket so you can collect a paper ticket at the station is not always possible; Aftersales are the ones to ask, and agents also said delivery method generally can’t be changed after purchase [#691018][#219597][#268207].

A screenshot is not an alternative — agents said the ticket needs to be on the phone [#701044]. If you travel without the ticket visible, you need a new ticket; leaving the phone behind was treated the same way [#633400].

This is from Virgin Trains’ Twitter support in October–December 2017 and may have changed since.

verification.feedback: No fix needed. Each substantive claim is said or fairly paraphrased by a Virgin Trains agent in at least one cited conversation; the 2017 note needs no support.

question: My Verizon Fios internet is down and the router still shows a red light after a reboot. What next?
reference_answer: VerizonSupport said to reboot the battery backup unit (BBU) by holding the Alarm Silence or Reset button for 15 seconds; it may beep and take a few minutes to reinitialize, so check the router after about 3 minutes.

answer.answer:
In 2017, when Fios internet was down and the router’s internet or globe light was still red after a reboot, Verizon agents gave these follow-ups. This is from those Twitter conversations and may have changed since.

They asked whether the WAN light on the back of the router was lit. [#77115] [#107122] Some also asked whether other services were down. [#362897] [#190838]

They had people reseat the coax and start the router again. One agent said to turn the router off, unscrew the coax, screw it back on, then restart the router. [#453871] Another said to unplug the router, unscrew the coax, wait 3 minutes, then reattach the coax and plug the router back in. [#668317]

If the light was still red, they had people reset the router. One said to push the reset pinhole on the back with a paperclip or toothpick and hold it until the front lights go off. [#453871] Another said to press and hold the reset button for 30 seconds with a paperclip. [#362897] If you had not changed settings such as the password, one agent asked for a factory reset. [#303576]

They also had people reboot the battery backup / ONT. Agents said the battery unit should be in the garage or a utility closet [#453871], and one described it as usually a black or white box with blue buttons, mounted on a wall in a closet or garage [#668317]. An agent said the ONT is the smaller unit on top, and to hold its Alarm Silence button to reboot it; that reboot takes a few minutes. [#214753] Button instructions they gave:
- Hold Alarm Silence for 30 seconds. [#453871]
- Hold Alarm Silence or ONT Reset for about 15 seconds. [#77115]
- Hold the blue ONT Reset for 15 seconds, or Alarm Silence for 15–20 seconds, then wait about 3 minutes and check the internet light. An agent said you may hear a beep. [#107122]
- Hold the ONT Reset for 15 seconds [#214753], or press the blue ONT Reset for about 10–15 seconds. If that button is not there, look for Alarm Silence, or a blue reset on the power supply. [#303576]
- Hold the blue ONT Reset for 20 seconds. [#668317]

When the light was still red after the router reset and the Alarm Silence or ONT Reset, agents asked the customer to follow and DM them. One said they would take a closer look. [#303576] [#107122] [#184321]

verification.feedback: No changes needed; each troubleshooting claim is said or fairly paraphrased by a Verizon agent in a cited conversation.

input.answer:
In late 2017, Verizon Fios agents treated a red internet/globe light that stayed red after a router reboot as a line/ONT issue, not something another router reboot would fix. Steps and hold times varied by agent, and equipment differs by home, so this is what they actually told customers—not a single official script. It may have changed since 2017.

What they asked people to try next:

1. Check the WAN light on the back of the router (and note whether TV/phone, if you have them, are also down). Agents wanted that light status before moving on. [#77115] [#107122]

2. Reseat the coax. Turn the router off, unscrew the coax connection, screw it back on, then restart the router. [#453871]

3. Hard-reset the router if the light is still red. On the back there is a reset pinhole (sometimes described as red). Hold it with a paperclip or toothpick until the front lights go off, or hold the reset button about 30 seconds. One agent only suggested a factory reset if you had not customized the router (for example, changed the password). [#453871] [#362897] [#303576]

4. Reboot the ONT from the battery backup unit (BBU). Agents said this is often in the garage, a utility closet, next to the router, or a smaller box on the wall (sometimes sitting on top of the BBU). Hold the Alarm Silence button about 15–30 seconds, or the blue ONT Reset button about 10–20 seconds, then wait a few minutes (one agent said about 3 minutes; you may hear a beep). The goal was for the router’s internet light to turn white and service to come back. This step fixed it for several people after a router reboot had not. [#453871] [#77115] [#107122] [#214753] [#303576]

question: After I signed in on a friend's PS4, my games show a content lock on my own console. How do I fix it?
reference_answer: AskPlayStation said the console has to be set as your primary PS4 to access the content, and to Restore Licenses and try again.

answer.answer:
In 2017 PlayStation Support treated a content lock (padlock) on games you own as a primary-console issue. Agents said an account can be activated as primary on only one PS4 at a time, and that the console has to be set as primary to access purchased content and remove the lock.

What they told people with locked games:

1. Activate your account as primary on the PS4 where you want to play. Agents said that is how you access content and remove the lock symbol.
2. Also restore licenses. One agent pointed to Settings → PlayStation Network → Restore Licenses. In a case matching this (“content lock because I logged on on my mates PS4”), support said the console needs to be set up as primary, then restore licenses and try again. When someone said the console was already primary and games were still locked, an agent suggested restoring licenses.
3. If this PS4 will not accept activation as primary because another console is already primary, agents said to deactivate all other consoles via PC (they sent a how-to link) and then reactivate this console as primary.
4. If verifying licenses doesn’t fix a lock and it says another user signed in, one agent said to sign out, sign in again, and activate as primary.

This is from Twitter support in October–December 2017, so the steps may have changed. When those fixes didn’t work, agents moved the conversation to Direct Message rather than posting more steps publicly.

verification.feedback: Each fix is a fair paraphrase of AskPlayStation’s own replies (one primary PS4, activate to clear the lock, Restore Licenses, deactivate other consoles via PC then reactivate, sign out/in). No change needed.

question: My internet is fast but my PS4 gets poor upload speeds even on a wired connection. Any fix?
reference_answer: After the general network tips, AskPlayStation suggested Safe Mode option 4 (Restore Default Settings) and then setting up the connection again.

answer.answer:
In October–November 2017, PlayStation support’s replies to low PS4 speeds—including customers who said upload stayed poor on a wired connection—were mostly links plus a few named steps. Agents did not spell those article steps out in the tweets, and this may have changed since 2017.

What agents actually told people:

- Use the steps in their article on improving the network/internet connection. [#501270] [#274965] [#288424] [#410357]
- Power-cycle network devices and try again. [#288424]
- Start the PS4 in Safe Mode and select Restore Default Settings. [#54399] [#288424] [#410357] In two of those chats this came after the customer said the improve-connection article had not fixed it [#410357], or after the improve-connection link and a power-cycle suggestion [#288424]. In the other, it was the only step given, after the customer said they had already reset the router and the PS4 and still had an upload problem only on the PS4. [#54399]
- Two agents were more specific: try Safe Mode option 4, Restore Default Settings, and set up the connection again. One said that after a customer reported they had already tried the improve-connection suggestions and still had poor upload on a wired connection. [#501270] The other said it after a customer reported a steep speed drop versus their PC and said they could not use a wired connection. [#395213]
- Asked whether Restore Default Settings would delete downloaded games, an agent said it will not delete saved data. [#410357]

Two further replies, not one sequence:

- After a customer said the improve-connection article did not help and the Ethernet connection was still unstable and slow, an agent said they may need to open firewall ports and linked more info. [#274965]
- In another chat, the customer reported that speeds improved after Restore Default Settings and then fell again (they reported about 555 kbps upload). The agent then said to refer to the port numbers in a linked list, and later moved the case to direct message. [#410357]

question: I paid for Wi-Fi on a Virgin Trains train and it doesn't work. What should I do?
reference_answer: VirginTrains suggested forgetting the network in your device settings, reconnecting, and following their link.

answer.answer:
In 2017, Virgin Trains agents told passengers whose paid onboard Wi-Fi wasn’t working to try a few fixes, then contact Wi-Fi support or claim a refund.

Troubleshooting they suggested:
- One agent asked whether the passenger was connected to the network named virgintrainswifi and had [link] open in a browser/tab [#649348].
- Another told a passenger to forget the network in their settings, reconnect, and follow [link] [#574203]. When that didn’t work, that same agent suggested speaking to the onboard team to see if they could reset the system. Earlier in that conversation they had asked whether the issue was speed or connection [#574203]. Other agents also asked if the problem was speed or connection, but did not go on to suggest an onboard reset [#81479][#403201].

If those steps didn’t help, agents gave the Wi-Fi support number 0330 088 1271 (also written 03300881271). One agent said that team could try to reset the connection [#743901]. Another gave the number without saying what the team would do [#574203]. A third said the team should be able to assist further [#403201]. A fourth said you can speak with the Wi-Fi team on that number regarding refunds if the Wi-Fi didn’t work [#174853].

For a refund or compensation when paid Wi-Fi failed, agents repeatedly said to email them (the address is redacted in these transcripts as __email__) [#649348][#81479][#574203][#403201]. One agent described it as a claim for compensation [#81479]; another said to contact that email for a full refund [#403201].

These replies are from October–November 2017, so the phone number, email, and process may have changed since.

verification.feedback: No fix needed. The troubleshooting steps, support number, refund/compensation email advice, and attributions match what Virgin Trains agents said in the cited conversations.

question: I spent a prestige token on the wrong weapon in Call of Duty WWII. Can Activision refund it?
reference_answer: No. ATVIAssist said prestige tokens can't be refunded.

answer.answer:
No. Activision’s support agents said they cannot refund or reverse a prestige token once it has been used, including when it was spent by accident on the wrong item in Call of Duty WWII.

In November 2017 they gave the same answer in several cases: they could not refund a token used on the Lee Enfield by accident [#432791], could not refund one used on a throwing knife [#439343], could not refund one used on a shovel the player didn’t want [#494620], and said that once a token has been used on an item (including a mis-click caused by a lagging menu), there is no way to reverse it or refund the token [#531761].

This is from Activision support conversations in 2017 and could have changed since.

verification.feedback: No fix needed. Each refusal is a fair paraphrase of an ATVIAssist statement in the cited 2017 conversations.

question: UPS says my package will arrive by 'end of day'. What time does that mean?
reference_answer: UPSHelp said end of day is 7 PM (delivery times run 9am to 7pm), though drivers can be out later in some areas.

answer.answer:
UPS support agents in 2017 did not treat “end of day” as a single fixed cutoff, and they gave slightly different answers.

Most often they said it means about 7:00 PM, with deliveries able to run later depending on the route, volume, or area. Agents described “end of the business day” as until around 7 pm, “typically around 07:00 PM,” or “End of day is 7 PM,” and said drivers usually finish about 7:00 PM but can be out later because of volume or local conditions ([#346702], [#213025], [#364368], [#752872]).

Other agents went later. One said drivers can be out as late as 10 PM, “if not later,” making delivery attempts ([#171101]). Another, asked whether “by end of day” means by midnight, said they try to be in before that but yes, midnight is the end of the day ([#397555]).

So in these 2017 replies, “end of day” was most commonly framed as around 7 PM, not a guarantee that the package would arrive by then—drivers could still deliver later, and at least one agent treated midnight as the end of the day. That guidance is from 2017 and may have changed.

question: Delta still hasn't found my delayed bag. Can I get reimbursed for things I buy in the meantime?
reference_answer: Yes. Delta said you can use the delayed-bag file you created to be reimbursed for purchases made while waiting for the bag.

answer.answer:
Yes. In 2017, Delta’s agents told customers whose bags were still delayed that they could seek reimbursement for things they bought while waiting.

Agents described this as reimbursement for “purchases while waiting,” “items re-purchased,” “interim expenses,” or “out of pocket expenses” due to the bag delay. Customers who raised clothes, toiletries, or a swimsuit were pointed to that same process. To claim, agents said to use the delayed-bag file you already opened, or a baggage claim form / the reimbursement link they provided, and to submit receipts and any supporting documentation.

It is not an automatic payout. When a customer said airport staff had refused reimbursement for any expenses while the bag was still delayed and they still needed to buy clothes, the Twitter agent did not confirm that refusal; they directed the customer to submit receipts and supporting documentation “for reimbursement consideration.” When asked for the exact policy, an agent pointed to a link rather than stating dollar limits or item rules in the tweet, so those details are not in this history.

After you file, agents said processing can take about 4–6 weeks, or 30–45 days for a response, and that you should get a notification on the claim. This is what Delta support said in October–December 2017 and may have changed since.

verification.feedback: No fix needed. Each claim is a fair paraphrase of what Delta agents said in the cited 2017 threads, and the 2017 caveat needs no citation.

question: Is McDonald's bringing back Szechuan sauce?
reference_answer: McDonald's said it isn't coming back for good, but would return for a third round in more US locations that winter; participating restaurants were listed through their link.

answer.answer:
Yes, according to McDonald’s support agents in fall 2017 — but not as a permanent item.

In early October 2017, agents said Szechuan Sauce was back on 10/7 at participating McDonald’s, while supplies last [#8686][#8494]. After that, they said the response was out of this world and they were bringing it back across the US that winter so more people could enjoy it [#64887].

They also clarified it was not coming back for good: it would return again that winter, for longer, with more sauce in more US locations, and told people to stay tuned [#57347][#65743]. As of 30 November 2017, when asked about a Christmas return, an agent still said it wasn’t coming back for good, but would be back that winter in larger quantities with more sauce available in all US locations, and to stay tuned — no specific date [#775524].

This is what agents said in October–November 2017 and may have changed since.

question: My Verizon Wi-Fi keeps dropping during online games. What can I do?
reference_answer: VerizonSupport said it may be wireless interference and suggested rebooting the router so it moves to another channel, then testing again.

answer.answer:
When customers reported losing games or Wi-Fi dropping, some Verizon agents in these 2017 chats said the problem may be wireless interference. One agent said that even with their best router, wireless will get interference from every neighbor and every nearby device, and that no one can prevent that [#429685]. Another said Verizon does not guarantee wireless connectivity because many factors can affect it [#133762].

What those agents told people to try:

- **Game over Ethernet.** They asked customers who were losing matches or having console trouble whether they had considered connecting the console to the router with an Ethernet cable. In an apartment-complex case, an agent said gaming wired may improve the experience because of interference [#429685]. They also suggested moving the router so the console could be wired, and said a furnace next to the equipment could cause interference [#572052] [#787934].

- **Reboot the router.** If they thought it was wireless interference, they told people to reboot the router so it would come up on another channel, then test again [#271121] [#133762]. For an Xbox whose Wi-Fi kept crashing, an agent also said the router needed to be reset [#787934].

- **Change the wireless channel.** Agents asked whether the customer had tried changing the channel to reduce interference [#135810]. They pointed to router login steps (2.4 GHz and 5 GHz set to Automatic; set either to a number that works better in the home) and compared it to changing a cordless-phone channel when you hear static [#606728]. They also sent a link to change the channel [#428048], told someone to try different channels and keep the one with the best speed [#250471], and, in one 2.4 GHz case, suggested trying channel 1, then channel 6, or just a channel different from the one in use [#649456].

- **Use their analyzer tools.** Agents mentioned a Wi-Fi analyzer in the My Fios app and told the customer to follow the on-screen steps [#250471]. They also asked whether the customer had tried the Wireless Wizard in “In Home Agent” [#133762].

- **Check the band and nearby radios.** They explained that some routers have a second network whose name ends in “5G,” with the password on the router label, if the device supports it [#135810]. They asked one customer to connect to 5 GHz, turn Bluetooth off, and send a speed-test result, and separately to turn Bluetooth off and retest [#75102]. They asked whether cordless phones, wireless speakers, baby monitors, or other radio-frequency devices were in the home, because those could cause interference [#649456].

- **Check distance, lights, and a wired speed test.** They asked whether the drop happened on all devices and how far those devices were from the router, and suggested a range extender when the router was in the basement [#135810]. They asked whether the internet light goes red when connectivity is lost [#271121], and when a customer said the lights sometimes turned red they still described it as possible wireless interference [#135810]. They asked for a speed test, said a wireless result can show interference, and said the best test is a wired test at the router [#75102] [#135810]. One agent also said to disconnect all devices except one and run a speed test [#135810].

- **Escalate if it continues.** If it was ongoing, an agent offered to send a technician [#606728]. In another chat, after asking whether the customer had Fios or DSL, an agent asked them to follow and send a DM so they could verify some information privately [#133762]. One agent asked a customer to factory-reset the router by holding the reset button on the back for 10 seconds [#75102].

This is only what Verizon agents said in October–December 2017. Equipment and their process may have changed since then.

verification.feedback: No changes needed. Each factual claim is said or fairly paraphrased by a Verizon agent in at least one cited 2017 conversation, and the 2017 date note needs no support.

WiFi keeps dropping change channel reboot router gaming
wireless interference disconnects during games what should I try
game console WiFi drops ethernet cable or change wireless channel

input.answer:
In late 2017, Verizon support agents treated Wi-Fi that drops during online games as a wireless-interference problem, not something they could fully prevent. They said wireless is affected by neighbors and nearby devices, that even their best router cannot stop that, and that they do not guarantee wireless connectivity because many factors can affect it [#429685] [#133762].

What they told people to try:

1. **Play wired if you can.** The most consistent advice for games was to plug the console into the router with an Ethernet cable instead of using Wi-Fi. Agents said that is more stable in apartments and condos, and they suggested moving the router if the cable would not reach [#429685] [#572052] [#787934]. A furnace or closet next to the router can also interfere [#572052].

2. **Reboot the router.** A reboot can put the Wi-Fi on a different channel. Agents asked people to try that and then test the connection again when games were dropping [#271121] [#133762] [#787934].

3. **Change the wireless channel yourself.** If a reboot is not enough, log into the router and set the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz channels off Automatic to a quieter number (agents compared it to changing a cordless-phone channel when you hear static). They also pointed people to the My Fios app’s Wi-Fi analyzer, or the Wireless Wizard in In Home Agent, and said to try different channels and keep the one with the best speed [#606728] [#135810] [#428048] [#250471] [#649456]. One agent specifically suggested trying channel 1 or 6 on 2.4 GHz if the current channel was crowded [#649456].

4. **Use 5 GHz if the console supports it.** Dual-band routers often show a second network whose name ends in “5G”; the password is on the router label. Agents preferred 5 GHz over 2.4 GHz when 2.4 was dropping or picking up interference [#135810] [#75102].

5. **Cut other radio noise.** Ask whether cordless phones, wireless speakers, baby monitors, or other radio devices are nearby [#649456]. They also told people to turn Bluetooth off, disconnect other devices (phones, tablets, laptops) while gaming, and run a speed test—ideally wired at the router—so they could tell interference from a line problem [#75102] [#135810].

6. **Check distance and the router lights.** If the router is far away (for example in the basement), they suggested a range extender [#135810]. When the connection drops, look at the router: if the internet light goes red, they treated that as more than ordinary Wi-Fi interference and wanted more detail [#271121] [#135810].

7. **If it keeps happening, escalate.** After those steps, agents offered a technician visit or asked the customer to follow and DM so they could look at the account [#606728] [#133762]. A factory reset (hold the reset button on the back about 10 seconds) was sometimes suggested, but at least one customer said it made things worse [#75102].

This is what Verizon agents said in October–December 2017. Router models, the My Fios app, and their process may have changed since then.

question: My Delta account got locked after too many failed login attempts. How do I get back in?
reference_answer: Delta said the account stays locked for 24 hours after the last failed attempt; after that you can try again, but more wrong attempts will lock it again.

answer.answer:
In late 2017, Delta agents said a SkyMiles account locked after too many failed logins unlocks itself after 24 hours, and Twitter agents generally cannot unlock it sooner.

Wait 24 hours from the last failed attempt (one agent said “exactly 24 hours after the initial security lock”), then use Forgot Password and follow the reset-email link. More wrong attempts will lock you out again. Agents said they cannot set a temporary password, and most said they have no way to speed up the unlock. [#461842] [#317108] [#412506] [#336794] [#339225] [#548132] [#523166] [#630401]

Some agents also gave a phone option: Online Support at 888-750-3284. The agent in [#91099] stressed that this is Online Support, not regular customer service. Another agent called it the Online Customer Support Desk at the same number and still said the account unlocks itself after 24 hours. [#168402]

Other replies varied. One agent sent a password-reset email and said password-procedure changes might require contacting SkyMiles Support with a copy of ID. [#512827] A few asked for the SkyMiles number by DM; one said locked accounts are not unlockable by an agent but offered to send a reset email, and another said they might be able to unlock it via DM. [#548132] [#512862] In one case a customer later reported that tech support had unlocked the account and sent a reset link without a 24-hour wait; the agent only said they were glad it was unlocked and did not confirm that as the process. [#630401] If you need to travel before the lock lifts, an agent said you can still book and then add your SkyMiles number to the reservation for credit. [#523166]

This is from October–November 2017 and may have changed.

verification.feedback: No fix needed. Each procedural claim is a fair paraphrase of a cited Delta agent, variations are attributed to the right conversations, and the customer’s no-wait unlock is correctly left unconfirmed.

question: Is there a way to get a more precise UPS delivery time than just 'out for delivery'?
reference_answer: UPSHelp recommended a free UPS My Choice account: set preferences, get updates, choose a two- or four-hour delivery window, and in some areas use Follow My Package.

answer.answer:
Yes. In late 2017, UPS agents said “out for delivery” on a typical end-of-day shipment does not include a specific time. Drivers are generally out from about 9 a.m. to 7 p.m., sometimes later because of volume. A more precise window was available only through certain options, and not on every package.

UPS My Choice (described as free) can sometimes show a 4-hour estimated delivery window. One agent said that estimate is based on past delivery history to your home. Agents described it as an estimate, not a guarantee, and said it is not always available. If My Choice or tracking does not show a window, that means one is not available for that package.

A narrower option is a 2-hour window through UPS My Choice Premium, or a purchased 2-hour confirmed window. One agent also said you can track the driver on express deliveries through that program. Agents described the 2-hour window as the time the driver is usually there; one said you would not be charged if that window was missed. For the 2-hour option, an agent said you may not have access until the day of delivery, and only if the local team is able to calculate the information.

If you need a committed time rather than an estimate, agents said end-of-day service levels do not have a delivery time. The shipper would need to use a service level with a guaranteed time (for example, an early-morning delivery, which can carry an extra fee).

This is what UPS support said in October–December 2017 and may have changed since.

verification.feedback: No fix needed. Each delivery-window claim is said by a UPS agent or is a fair paraphrase, and the 2017 caveat does not need a citation.

question: How do I get the passenger charter discount when renewing my GWR season ticket?
reference_answer: GWRHelp said that if the season ticket was bought at a station you renew at the same ticket office; if it was bought online you renew online and then email them to claim the discount.

input.query: passenger charter discount renewing season ticket
email to claim renewal discount season ticket passenger charter
how to claim season ticket renewal discount online email
email upon online renewal claim discount season ticket
passenger charter discount not applied when renewing
renew season ticket at same ticket office discount not showing online
what email address to claim renewal discount season ticket
return to the point of purchase season ticket renewal discount
annual season ticket passenger charter discount how to get it

email gwr.feedback renewal discount claim after renewing online
