need to email after renewing season ticket online to get discount
bring old season ticket to ticket office to get discount applied
weekly season ticket renewal discount or delay repay compensation
punctuality reliability targets not met renewal discount percentage 5% or 10%

input.answer:
In GWR’s 2017 Twitter replies, the passenger charter discount is the renewal discount for monthly or longer season tickets when punctuality and/or reliability targets in the Passenger’s Charter are missed. It is not compensation for individual delays; agents said those claims are for daily or weekly tickets, and monthly or longer tickets are compensated only by this renewal discount [#715605] [#174318].

How agents said to get it when you renew:

1. Check whether a discount is actually due for your route before you renew. Agents pointed people to GWR’s performance figures and applicable-discounts page; you do not have to go in person to find out, and the discount does not appear on National Rail planners or at the online payment screen [#95900] [#376343] [#742164] [#286943]. In late 2017 the amount they quoted was usually 5%, and 10% only if both punctuality and reliability targets were missed [#174318]. The windows were route- and period-specific — for example 5% on some routes for renewals between 22 October and 18 November 2017, and on London–Thames Valley routes between 19 November and 16 December 2017 [#310346] [#233333] [#646391]. Those dates were for 2017 only.

2. Renew within 28 days of the ticket expiring, or the discount is not given even if it is being offered [#370473].

3. Agents did not all describe the same process for applying it:
   - Several said that if it is due it is applied automatically when you renew and you do not need to apply. Natalie said that for a ticket bought at a station it is applied automatically at the ticket office [#667046] [#822644] [#507928] [#309325].
   - Jordan, answering someone who could not see the passenger charter discount at online checkout, said you must return to the point of purchase: the same ticket office if the current ticket was bought at a station. You can only claim the renewal discount online if the original ticket was bought online, and in that case you need to email after the online renewal because the discount is not taken off at payment [#286943]. That thread did not give the email address.

If you do not renew, agents disagreed: Jordan said no compensation is due because the discount is only offered on renewal [#687628]; Lewis said to contact Customer Support 28 days after expiry and they may send the discount as a cheque instead [#732619].

This is what GWR agents said in October–December 2017 and may have changed since.

question: My suitcase came off a Delta flight ripped to shreds. How do I file a claim?
reference_answer: Delta sent a claim form (completing it gives you a file reference number). When the form wouldn't submit, they said to call Baggage Service at 1-800-325-8224, open 24/7, to file the claim.

answer.answer:
Delta agents in 2017 treated a ripped suitcase as a damaged-baggage claim, but they did not all give the same steps. The usual instruction was to take the bag to a Delta Baggage Service Office so an agent can inspect it and open the claim.

What most agents said:
- Bring the suitcase to the Baggage Service Office at the arriving airport (or the nearest one) so staff can review the damage and create a Damaged Bag Report / claim. They said damage could not be verified over Twitter and the bag had to be looked at by a Delta representative. [#270055] [#674369] [#442623] [#603021] [#803795] [#1677] [#557834]
- Report it within 24 hours for U.S. travel and within 7 days for international travel. Some agents said this should be immediately after arrival, before you leave the airport, and within 24 hours of the flight even if the office was empty when you landed. One agent added that an individual airport may make exceptions. [#331989] [#803795] [#603021] [#1677] [#775189] [#557834]
- The online claim form usually asks for a file reference number from the Baggage Service Center or an airport agent. Agents said you can check a claim’s status online, but you generally cannot start the claim online without that number. [#331989] [#122271] [#739088] [#775189]

Phone option some agents gave: call the Baggage Service Center at (800) 325-8224. One agent said they are open 24/7 and you can file with them by phone; others said call them to get the file reference number before using the form. The same number was also given as the Anchorage baggage-office line, staffed 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 a.m. daily, with the ticket counter upstairs when that office is closed. [#328704] [#739088] [#122271] [#331989]

Agents did not always agree. Some told people they could be reimbursed by writing Baggage or by filling out an online claim or complaint form (one path described was “voice a complaint” → Baggage → damaged), and one said completing the form would itself generate a file reference number. In one conversation, an agent called earlier advice to file online misinformation and said the bag had to be inspected at the airport before a claim could be filed. [#707369] [#328704] [#511405] [#610566] [#774188] [#331989]

This is what Delta agents said in 2017; the process, deadlines, and phone number may have changed.

verification.feedback: No changes needed. Each procedural claim is a fair paraphrase of a Delta agent in the conversations cited for that point, including the conflicting online-form advice.

question: Does GWR offer information or announcements in Welsh?
reference_answer: GWRHelp said Welsh literature is available on request and some staff may make announcements in Welsh.

answer.answer:
Yes, but only in a limited way, according to GWR’s Twitter agents in October–December 2017. This may have changed since.

Agents said literature can be made available in Welsh on request. Andy stated this several times and also said nothing had changed from the older HST fleet ([#294862], [#294275], [#296691], [#296509], [#311278], [#284043]). Lewis said once that Welsh literature is available upon request ([#310156]). If you email Customer Support and say what you need, they can send it; you don’t have to address the email to a named person ([#311278]).

On announcements, Andy said individual staff members can make announcements in Welsh ([#294862]), and Lewis said some staff may do so ([#310156]) — not that Welsh announcements are standard on every train. When customers asked why new trains had no Welsh announcements or bilingual signage, Andy said nothing had changed regarding Welsh signage/announcements and pointed to literature on request instead ([#294275], [#296691], [#296509], [#311278]). Requests for routine Welsh announcements or bilingual signage were passed on as feedback, not confirmed as something they would provide ([#307803], [#308134], [#311278]).

Separately, when a customer asked for a copy of GWR’s Welsh language policy in Welsh, Lewis directed them to the Customer Support email ([#302665]). In a later conversation, Josh said GWR was in regular contact with the Welsh Assembly and pointed to a current policy (the link itself isn’t in the tweet text) ([#789794]).

verification.feedback: No fix needed. Each claim is backed by a GWR agent in at least one cited conversation, or is a fair paraphrase of what they said.
